name: Basilica of Saint Mary
history: Archbishop John Ireland announced a pro-cathedral for Minneapolis in 1903 and hired Emmanuel Masqueray, who was also designing the Cathedral of Saint Paul. Ground was broken in 1907 and 30,000 people came to the cornerstone ceremony in 1908. Dedicated in 1913, it became the first basilica in the United States when Pius XI granted the title in 1926. It is co-cathedral of the archdiocese.
arch: Beaux-Arts in white Vermont granite on a Rockville granite base, with a colonnaded portico between two 116-foot spires and a great dome over the sanctuary.
features: The dome rises 138 feet inside; with its lantern and 62-foot cross it reaches 200 feet.
It has nine shrines, or side altars.

look.d: The lantern and cross bring the dome to a total height of 200 feet.
The 116-foot spires frame the portico on Hennepin Avenue.

fun: This was the very first minor basilica in the United States.
journal: America's first basilica: white granite in Minneapolis, a dome and two spires.
